subject.title: fix(agents): tighten bash-tools schema fields from Type.Number to Type.Integer

question: Should the documented `exec.yieldMs` tool parameter become integer-only, or should this repair remain limited to non-negative process-log pagination fields?
rationale: The process pagination fields have clear line/count semantics and a proof-positive canonical PR, but current docs expose `yieldMs` as a general millisecond number and the repository does not establish that rejecting fractional callers is intended.

options.title: Keep `yieldMs` numeric
options.body: Preserve the existing exec contract and use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/105560 as the canonical non-negative `offset`/`limit` repair.

options.title: Approve integer-only `yieldMs`
options.body: Retain the additional tightening only after adding direct exported-schema tests, real after-fix proof, and explicit contract documentation.

options.title: Normalize at runtime
options.body: Keep the public schema compatible and explicitly normalize finite `yieldMs` values at the runtime boundary if sub-millisecond input is unsupported.

recommendation.title: Keep `yieldMs` numeric
recommendation.body: Preserve the existing exec contract and use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/105560 as the canonical non-negative `offset`/`limit` repair.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a public agent-tool contract and compatibility choice in an area with substantial recent exec/runtime ownership from this contributor.
